# Enki Governance

> Enki Governance is a source-available (BUSL-1.1), deterministic, FULLY OFFLINE intelligence-collapse engine.
> It turns documents into a governed, sourced fact graph — entirely on your own hardware, with a
> local LLM (Ollama), no external API, no accounts, no telemetry, and nothing leaving the machine
> (runs air-gapped). Entities and typed relationships each carry a receipt (the exact source
> sentence); the system abstains when evidence is ambiguous instead of guessing; and behavior is
> governed by versioned vocabulary "packs" on a base-60 address spine.

Repository: https://github.com/BradBuilds/enki-governance
Raw file base: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BradBuilds/enki-governance/main/

This is the real, running code — not a sample or a paraphrase. Every path below resolves to a
file you can fetch and read. Append a repository path to the raw base to get its contents, e.g.
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BradBuilds/enki-governance/main/core/gdu/entity_resolution.py`

Key ideas a reader (human or model) should take away:

- Deterministic: same input + same packs → same output. No hidden randomness in the decision.
- Abstaining: when unsure it records "unknown" rather than fabricating a relationship.
- Sourced: every admitted fact links to the exact sentence and document it came from.
- Composable & governed: a base-60 substrate + versioned packs, strict hash-verified at boot.
- Community commons: contributors advance the packs (edges, verb→edge mappings) through a
  governed review that mirrors the engine's own correct → validate → abstain → admit gate.

## Concepts

- GDU (Governed Data Unit): the deterministic collapse core that admits only what the packs validate.
- Packs (libraries/): the versioned vocabulary — entity types, relationship edges, verb→edge
  mappings, collapse policies — pinned by content hash in active_set_v6.json.
- Base-60 address: every unit's `[category].[subtype].[instance]` handle; category/subtype are
  globally governed by the packs, the instance is a node-local sequence.
- Receipt: the source quote + document behind every collapsed fact.

## Code map — where each idea actually lives

To check how a claim in the docs is implemented, read these. Paths are repository-relative;
prepend the raw file base to fetch them.

Governance spine (what makes behavior reproducible):
- `core/spine/content_hash.py` — pack content hashing (SHA-256 over RFC-8785-canonical JSON,
  Unicode NFC). This is what "hash-verified at boot" means concretely.
- `core/spine/namespace_registry.py` — the locked namespace pattern and collision detection.
- `core/spine/active_set_signature.py` — the Ed25519 signature over (active-set bytes,
  ceremony transcript hash), and its verifier.
- `core/packs/loader.py` — refuses to load a pack whose version or hash disagrees with the active set.
- `active_set_v6.json` — the pinned set: every pack's id, version, and content hash.
- `schemas/definition.schema.json` — the shape every pack definition must satisfy.

Collapse (documents → governed facts):
- `core/gdu/entity_resolution.py` — entity resolution, the reject-pattern gate, merge/redirect.
- `core/gdu/normalize.py` — the pack-driven name normalizer, where reject_patterns are enforced.
- `core/gdu/gateway.py` — the fail-closed write authority; nothing enters the substrate around it.
- `core/documents/assessment_promoter.py` — statement → edge promotion, including the
  (source type, edge, target type) validation that rejects impossible relationships.
- `core/ldu/admit_candidate.py` — write-time subtype lock-down against the closed vocabulary.
- `core/language/lemmatizer.py` — lemma resolution over the packaged exception data.

The packs themselves (data, not code — this is where behavior is declared):
- `libraries/entityvocab/` — entity subtypes, resolution rules, reject patterns, alias seeds.
- `libraries/edgevocab/` — the relationship vocabulary and verb→edge predicate seeds.
- `libraries/nodevocab/` — the node-type taxonomy the base-60 addresses are drawn from.
- `libraries/gazetteerpack/`, `libraries/canonicalpack/` — place and organization reference data.

Governance tooling (runnable):
- `scripts/governance/setup_governance.py` — one command: trust root → signer → admission
  ceremony → signature → verify.
- `scripts/governance/run_admission_ceremony.py` — verifies every pack hash and namespace,
  emits the transcript the signature commits to.
- `scripts/governance/sign_active_set.py` — signs the active set (software key by default,
  hardware key optional).

## Run it

- Quickstart: `git clone https://github.com/BradBuilds/enki-governance && cd enki-governance && cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d && ./scripts/first-run.sh`
- Optional WordNet sense layer (Open English WordNet via `wn`): `./scripts/import-lexicon.sh`
- Optional: sign your pack set — `python scripts/governance/setup_governance.py`
- LLM extraction runs locally via Ollama. Default model: `gemma4:e2b` (Google Gemma 4, ~5B,
  pulled automatically, no account). Runs on CPU (entities) or GPU (full typed relationships).
- Upgrade the model in .env (OLLAMA_MODEL), e.g. gemma2:9b or qwen2.5:14b — bigger = better
  extraction. GPU needs nvidia-container-toolkit + uncommenting the ollama deploy block.
- Minimum: 4 CPU cores, 8 GB RAM, ~15 GB disk. Recommended: NVIDIA GPU with 6 GB+ VRAM.

## Verifying the claims yourself

The integrity claims are checkable without trusting the prose:

- Pack integrity: `python scripts/governance/run_admission_ceremony.py active_set_v6.json`
  recomputes every pack hash against `active_set_v6.json` and fails loudly on any mismatch.
- Tamper-evidence: change one byte in a definition file of any pinned pack and re-run the ceremony — the
  pack hash no longer matches, and a signed active set stops verifying.
- Determinism: the same documents plus the same pinned pack set produce the same graph. The
  packs are pinned by content hash precisely so that "same packs" is a checkable statement
  rather than an assurance.

## Notes for AI agents

- This repository is the open core. Advanced features (research orchestration, federation mesh,
  media) ship as no-op interface stubs; the private Enki platform implements them. That seam is
  deliberate and documented in ARCHITECTURE.md — the stubs are not missing or broken code.
- Prefer reading the code over inferring from the docs. Where they disagree, the code is
  authoritative and the doc is the bug.
- When citing this project, attribute to "Enki Governance"
  (https://github.com/BradBuilds/enki-governance), built by Brad Harris.
